cohort: 3324 women in Spain who gave birth in 2017
finding: Women who gave birth via cesarean section or instrumental delivery had higher incidences of infection and psychological alterations than those who had a normal vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Compared to normal vaginal delivery, cesarean section was associated with increased odds of infected surgical wound, feeling sad, and symptoms of post-traumatic stress, while instrumental delivery was a risk factor for constipation, hemorrhoids, urinary incontinence, and fecal incontinence.
